CV.1: Knowing peak from average tells you whether a sound is truly quiet or just spiky, which decides how you level it.
CV.2: Thinking in times instead of units makes every fader, meter and compressor setting you meet later easy to predict.
CV.3: Meters cannot hear, so balancing a bass against a lead takes your ears, with the numbers as a check.
CV.4: Layering two sounds can add a lot, a little or cancel outright, and this is how you know which to expect.
CV.5: A wave that looks different is not always a different sound, which saves you chasing changes that are only pictures.
CV.6: The spectrogram is the one view that shows movement, so it is how you study sweeps, wobbles and hits.
CV.7: Once you can spot jumps and corners you can guess how bright any wave will be before you play it.
CV.8: Sweeping a narrow band is a way to find exactly which harmonic is ringing or missing in any sound you make.
